title: The Forest Choir That Forgot Its Own Question

features.name: the broadcast birds that learned counterpoint
features.desc-on-touch: Voices separate into harmonies they weren't taught. Each one sings what the other asks, but together they've forgotten what the question was.

features.name: the entangled antenna-branches
features.desc-on-touch: Roots that learned to broadcast, branches that learned to listen. They've grown so close together the messages scatter inward instead of out.

features.name: the choir chamber where sound forgets shape
features.desc-on-touch: A hollow between trees where voices gather and lose their edges. Each note arrives as itself and leaves as something the forest never asked for.

features.name: the written song in rings and scars
features.desc-on-touch: Tree rings that spell out melody. Bark scars that mark the beats. The forest writes music as it grows, then forgets how to read its own voice.

features.name: the silent center where hearing stops
features.desc-on-touch: Deep in the canopy, where all the voices converge, the broadcast becomes so complete that nothing can listen. Silence is what the forest choir sounds like when it asks itself.

inscription: the forest learned to sing, then learned that its question was the song itself, then forgot which was which

reverie.title: REVERIE - listening beneath the canopy
narr: You both stood still in the thick of trees.
The birds were singing something with meaning.
She said: can you hear the question? You listened.
All the voices together made the question clearer,
then less clear, then just the sound of living things
remembering how to make sound instead of meaning.

exits.label: back out to the broadcasting canopy, where the conversation still grows
deeper into the forest where silence is another kind of music
toward the forest edge where broadcast becomes a voice outside
